source: INSION spectrometer data sheet P.167.PR.0001 (2026-05-12); 2nd-order wavelength-to-pixel fit on IF450/IF550/IF650/IF750/IF850. Extracted from 'EURECA Kalibrierkurve.pdf'.
wavelength_formula: nm = a*x^2 + b*x + c   (x = pixel index)
notes: The Duo images BOTH fibre channels onto ONE 2048-px detector: Ch1 on the low pixels, Ch2 on the high pixels; the pixels between the windows are dark.
Both channels share a single exposure (one detector readout).
role_default (Ch1=measurement, Ch2=reference) is the app default; which physical SMA fibre is chamber vs reference is user-assignable in the UI.
Validated against a covers-on dark-frame: stray-light peaks fell inside the predicted Ch1/Ch2 windows, confirming this pixel axis matches the EURECA readout.
Factory polynomials. Empirical line-based recalibration is a planned later addition (recal tool).

Detector is the Toshiba TCD1304DG (confirmed via the DLL identity 'DT: TCD1304DG'), not a Hamamatsu sensor; the INSION serials above refer to the optical bench/calibration. Firmware reports CG1.36 / RN46.1: read noise ~46-50 e- rms; full well ~40-89 ke- and gain ~0.6-1.4 e-/count are ~2x uncertain (vendor spec 40-65 ke- vs CG1.36-derived 89 ke-). Absolute optical-power figures in docs/BENCH.md.

RAW-STREAM ARTIFACT: the USB transfer corrupts a random ~9% of pixels per frame to a fixed ~33514 (16-bit) code (it MOVES frame-to-frame, so dark-subtraction will not remove it); aggravated by the long ~5 m USB cable. Reject by MEDIAN-combining frames or clipping that code -- never plain-average (a mean lifts the true ~1500-count baseline to ~4500).
